learning_outcomes.text: Be able to solve mechanical problems applying vectorial, analytical and energetic methods.
Be able to prepare technical reports to explain theoretical-experimental work in the field of mechanics.
Be able to create a mathematical model to simulate the mechanical behavior of mechanical systems in equilibrium and in motion.
Be able to formulate and solve the equations of mechanics applied to kinematic and dynamic problems of planar and three-dimensional mechanisms and machines.
Be able to formulate and solve the equations of mechanics applicable to equilibrium problems of structural systems and cables.
Know the principles of analytical mechanics and its application to problems of structures and machines.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of articulated structures with loads at the nodes
Analysis of articulated structures with intermediate loads on the bars. Machine analysis.
Principle of Virtual Work for static analysis
Internal forces in beams and cables
Types of loads and supports in beams
General plane motion. Instantaneous center of rotation.
Introduction to Analytical Mechanics for Dynamic Analysis
L1. Introduction to experimentation in mechanical engineering.
L2. Introduction to simulation in mechanical engineering.
L3. Static simulation of the behavior of structures.
L4. Experimental verification of the effect of friction.
L5. Dynamic simulation of machine operation.

assessment_methods.method: Written theoretical-practical tests during the course

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must achieve a minimum global average of 5 out of 10 points. In the first attempt, the final exam (70%) requires a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 points; otherwise, the global grade cannot exceed 4.5. Continuous assessment (laboratory work 10%, written tests 20%) has no minimum grade. In the second attempt, the final exam (90%) also requires a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 points, with the same restriction on the global grade if not met, and laboratory work contributes 10%. Laboratory practices are not recoverable due to limited resources. Fraudulent activity in any assessment will result in a 0 for that activity or the entire exam, with possible further sanctions.
